sources.quote: both IRCC and the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants tell prospects to check a representative on the CICC Public Register
sources.title: Spot, stop, report: Taking action against immigration fraud - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: To protect yourself, follow three steps: spot warning signs such as pressure to act quickly, requests for large cash payments or guaranteed results, stop before you act and verify information on Canada.ca, and confirm that your immigration representative is authorized. Citizenship or immigration consultants must be a member of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants. The College maintains a public register of licensed consultants.

sources.quote: IRCC has capped study permits at up to 408,000 for 2026, roughly 16 percent below the 2024 target
sources.title: 2026 provincial and territorial allocations under the international student cap - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: For 2026, IRCC expects to issue up to 408,000 study permits, including 155,000 to newly arriving international students and 253,000 extensions for current and returning students. This number is 7% lower than the 2025 issuance target of 437,000 and 16% lower than the 2024 issuance target of 485,000.

sources.quote: Planned provincial nominee admissions for 2026 sit well above the level set in the previous plan
sources.title: Supplementary Information for the 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Targets for new temporary resident arrivals are set at 385,000 in 2026 and 370,000 in 2027 and 2028. The Plan increases admissions under the Federal High Skilled and Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), ensuring that Canada is able to attract the talent needed while also responding to the distinct labour market needs of provinces and territories. Overall permanent resident admissions will stabilize at 380,000 from 2026 to 2028.

sources.quote: Marketing must not guarantee the success of an application, must not be misleading, and must not imply a relationship with or special influence over IRCC
sources.title: Code of Professional Conduct for College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Licensees
sources.evidence: In marketing immigration or citizenship consulting services, a licensee must not make false, misleading or inaccurate representations, guarantee the success of an application, expression of interest or proceeding, or imply that the licensee has a relationship with the Government of Canada or of a province.

sources.quote: only authorized representatives may be paid to advise or represent on an IRCC matter: CICC licensees in good standing, lawyers and paralegals licensed by a provincial law society, and Quebec notaries
sources.title: Find out if your representative is authorized - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Authorized representatives are members in good standing of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC), lawyers and paralegals who are members in good standing of a Canadian provincial or territorial law society, and notaries who are members in good standing of the Chambre des notaires du Québec. If you pay a representative or compensate them in any way in exchange for their services, they are considered paid and must be authorized.

sources.quote: A consultant handling Quebec immigration procedures must also be recognized by the provincial ministry and listed on the Registre quebecois des consultants en immigration
sources.publisher: Gouvernement du Québec (Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration)
sources.title: Qui doit obtenir la reconnaissance comme consultant en immigration | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: Holding a valid permit from the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants is not sufficient to act as an immigration consultant in Quebec. You must obtain recognition from the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration if you receive remuneration to advise, assist or represent a person in presenting an immigration application. When you obtain recognition, your name appears in the Registre québécois des consultants en immigration.

sources.quote: Competition Act deceptive marketing provisions cover drip pricing
sources.title: Drip pricing - Competition Bureau Canada
sources.evidence: Drip pricing involves offering a product or service at a price that is unattainable because consumers must also pay additional charges or fees. In 2022, the Government of Canada amended the Competition Act to explicitly recognize drip pricing as a deceptive business practice: representing a price that a customer cannot actually attain because there are mandatory fixed additional charges or fees is a false or misleading representation.

sources.quote: a newly announced category such as the 2026 stream for internationally trained physicians
sources.title: Canada prioritizes top talent in 2026 immigration Express Entry categories - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: In February 2026, Canada introduced a new Express Entry category for foreign medical doctors with Canadian work experience: international doctors with at least one year of Canadian work experience in an eligible occupation, gained within the last three years. The first round for foreign medical doctors with Canadian work experience was announced for the coming days following the February 18, 2026 announcement.

sources.quote: Local Services Ads, and the verification badge attached to them, have been limited to home service categories in Canada rather than professional services
sources.title: Getting started with Local Services Ads - Canada - Local Services Help
sources.evidence: Local Services Ads are available only for certain service categories. Home services include providers like locksmiths, cleaners, painters, landscapers, or others who service private residences and businesses. Eligible categories listed for Canada include appliance repair, garage door, house cleaning, HVAC, lawn care and locksmiths.
